country.comment: Examines municipally owned and operated drinking water systems across the contiguous United States (Alaska and Hawaii are excluded because they lack conventional municipally owned and operated systems).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 4, Section 3.1 & Figure 1

effect_estimate.comment: Headline quantitative findings from descriptive statistics and the combined OLS regression with state fixed effects (n = 2,119 municipalities, state-clustered robust SEs).
effect_estimate.value: Across 2,119 US municipalities, the monthly household cost of basic drinking water services (6,000 gal/month including fixed charges and volumetric rates) averaged $38.60 (range $5.00 to $163.40; ~3.3% of gross monthly income at the $7.25/h federal minimum wage). In the combined state fixed effects OLS model (n = 2,119, R2 = 0.29, adjusted R2 = 0.271), higher monthly basic water costs were associated with wholesale purchased water reliance (b = 2.86, SE = 0.91, p < 0.05; +$2.86/month), surface water vs. groundwater source (b = 5.50, SE = 0.87, p < 0.01; +$5.50/month), per-capita water utility expenditures (b = 0.0055, SE = 0.00080, p < 0.01), municipal debt ratio (b = 0.40, SE = 0.24, p < 0.10), and population density (b = 0.00056, SE = 0.00017, p < 0.01). Lower monthly basic water costs were associated with logged population size (b = -2.08, SE = 0.41, p < 0.01), conservative resident political ideology (b = -5.44, SE = 2.41, p < 0.05), and percent Hispanic population (b = -0.095, SE = 0.025, p < 0.01). Mayor form of government was associated with lower monthly water costs in the organizational model (b = -1.58, SE = 0.69, p < 0.05) but not statistically significant in the combined model (b = -1.03, SE = 0.76), and recent EPA SDWA health-based violations had no significant effect (b = 0.96, SE = 0.86).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 6, Table 2; PDF p. 7, Section 4; PDF p. 8, Table 3

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional OLS regression documenting statistical associations between municipal institutional/fiscal/regulatory characteristics (rate-setting, mayor vs. manager governance, wholesale water purchasing, utility debt/spending, SDWA violations) and household monthly water bills; capped below 3 by observational cross-sectional design and does not directly observe the administrative rate-setting mechanism operating on household access (1 = documented statistical association).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 5–6, Sections 3.1–3.5; PDF p. 7–8, Section 4 & Table 3

mechanism_flags.comment: Focuses on municipal drinking water rate-setting (fixed charges and volumetric water fees/tariffs) across a decentralized/fragmented municipal utility landscape, including organizational governance form (mayor vs. council-manager) and wholesale water purchasing contracts.
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2–3, Sections 2–2.3; PDF p. 5, Sections 3.1 & 3.4; PDF p. 10, Section 6

outcome_flags.comment: Primary outcome is the monthly household cost (bill) for basic drinking water services (6,000 gal/month), analyzed as a direct component of household water affordability and benchmarked against federal minimum-wage monthly income; recent EPA SDWA health-based water quality violations are included only as an independent variable.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 2; PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; PDF p. 6–7, Table 2 & Section 4

publication_year.comment: Published in 2025 in AWWA Water Science (Received 4 December 2023; Revised 19 November 2024; Accepted 27 December 2024; © 2025).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Quantitative cross-sectional observational study estimating OLS regressions across municipalities (using cross-sectional water rates collected Nov 2021–May 2022 matched to municipal covariates with state fixed effects), with no longitudinal intervention or quasi-experimental comparator.
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 3–6, Sections 3.1–3.5; PDF p. 8, Table 3

sample_size.comment: Rate schedules were collected for 2,161 US municipalities (population >= 10,000 owning and operating a drinking water system); complete-case main OLS regressions analyze n = 2,119 municipalities, and Appendix Table A1 sensitivity models incorporating presidential vote share analyze n = 2,003 municipalities.
sample_size.value: 2,161 municipalities with drinking water rate data collected; 2,119 municipalities in main regression analysis (2,003 municipalities in presidential vote share sensitivity models)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 & Section 3.3; PDF p. 6, Table 2; PDF p. 8, Table 3; PDF p. 12, Table A1

study_design.comment: Cross-sectional municipal-level dataset combining original rate collection (Nov 2021–May 2022) with the Municipal Drinking Water Database (MDWD), analyzed via OLS regression models with state fixed effects (and EPA regional fixed effects in sensitivity analyses) and state-clustered robust standard errors.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional observational study using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with state-level fixed effects
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Section 1; PDF p. 3–6, Sections 3.1–3.5; PDF p. 8, Table 3
